title: ISSM: initialize from a MAT file
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: 1. Prepare your files and access
instructions: Open Pilot Tutorials → Upload a dataset → download the native initial-condition packet. Extract it.
Have an approved login, connected AWS resources and configured MATLAB/Connector. Choose Cloud → Advanced → ISSM.
steps.why: Full geometry and velocity fields must initialize the actual native mesh.
steps.expected: Four scripts + issm-shelf-initial.mat; verified BYO AWS, MATLAB and Connector.
steps.note: Scripts: native-data-issm-mat/ (all four files). Data: datasets/issm-shelf-initial.mat. Prerequisites are linked on the tutorial page.

steps.title: 2. Create an owned example
instructions: In Editor, enter a new name and choose New example.
This recording uses pilot-issm-mat-1119. A new ISSM example can include a seeded runme.m that must be replaced with your real script.
The blue confirmation says the workspace example was created.
Keep this owned example selected while uploading and referencing the input. Source files and datasets use different controls.
steps.why: An owned example keeps your imported workflow separate from installed examples. Source imports and dataset attachments must belong to the same example.
steps.expected: Expected: the newly created workspace name.
steps.note: A seeded runme.m must be replaced by the supplied MAT run script before launch. This is an editable workspace example, separate from the read-only application examples.

steps.title: 3. Upload the MAT file
instructions: Scroll below Environment & resources in the left column to Datasets. Choose issm-shelf-initial.mat, then choose Upload. The selected-file count changes from 1 to 0 after upload.
This is a synthetic 5×9 gridded field file for a 10 km square shelf.
steps.why: The MAT file contains the full synthetic initial-condition grids.
steps.expected: Expected: one selected file becomes Uploaded: issm-shelf-initial.mat.
steps.note: Upload stores the file. The script and schema-specific reader must still load it.

steps.title: 4. Reference the staged filename
instructions: Select issm-shelf-initial.mat and choose Reference in example. Keep the baseline filename.
The confirmation gives data/issm-shelf-initial.mat. The run script must read that exact relative path.
steps.why: Referencing provides the exact relative path that runme.m reads.
steps.expected: Expected: data/issm-shelf-initial.mat; do not add data/ twice.
steps.note: Do not add data/ twice. Referencing makes the bytes available; it does not start the model.

steps.title: 5. Import all four source files
instructions: Choose runme.m, Launch.par, validate_launch_dataset.m and load_initial_conditions.m together.
Check Replace existing script files for the seeded runme.m, then choose Import script files.
The confirmation names all four imported files and says Files are saved.
The imported runme.m is now the actual MAT reader/ISSM workflow. All four script hashes were verified before launch and in the submitted snapshot.
steps.why: Replacement updates the new example’s starter runme.m. Only saved scripts enter the next run snapshot.
steps.note: The actual continuous take shows selected count 4, replacement enabled, the import action and then count 0. All four filenames must appear in the saved-file confirmation before you continue.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the entry script
instructions: In Experiment, confirm Action = Run and Run target = runme.m.
Importing source files does not select a different target or submit an AWS job.
Choose Review & Launch. Confirm model ISSM and example pilot-issm-mat-1119, readiness and resources.
Scroll to the bottom of the review and choose Launch cloud run explicitly.
steps.why: The entrypoint chooses the MATLAB workflow that will execute. Review checks resources, readiness, configured license and Connector.
steps.note: The four saved scripts and the referenced MAT file must all be present before review. Check 2 vCPU / 8 GiB and the existing license/Connector. Measured execution times appear in the completion card.

steps.title: 7. Watch the new submission
instructions: Confirm Launch cloud run at the bottom of the review.
Watch the MAT experiment progress through Staging/Submitting, then wait for Queued, Running and Completed.
steps.why: The new submission is the run to monitor through completion.
steps.expected: Expected: Staging/Submitting, then Queued, Running and Completed.
steps.note: The manifest links the actual saved source/data, pinned image, job and retained archive.

steps.title: 8a. Initial thickness
instructions: Initial thickness is 300–500 m.
The axes span a 10 km square in metres.
Surface elevation is in metres.
This floating shelf uses consistent thickness, base and surface.
Initial speed is in metres/year.
The next diagnostic solve computes the native velocity field.
steps.why: The saved native figure shows the uploaded fields on the Triangle mesh. Floating-shelf base and surface must remain consistent with thickness. The diagnostic solver then computes the native velocity response.
steps.expected: Initial speed uses metres/year; this is not a transient time plot.
steps.note: Exact saved native PNG, shown as the complete three-panel strip; this panel is outlined without stretching or altering pixels.

steps.title: 9. Verify initialization and completion
instructions: Initialized thickness, base, surface, vx and vy match the uploaded file at all 13 native vertices, with maximum error 0.
One diagnostic SSA Stressbalance solve completed; no physical time advances.
steps.why: A file upload is useful only when its fields actually initialize the model.
steps.expected: All five fields × 13 native vertices: interpolation error 0.
steps.note: Startup 220.723 s · AWS task 51.018 s · script 9.568328 s, including setup, mesh, initial plotting and solving.

steps.title: 10. Render the current velocity field
instructions: Open Workspace → Results for the completed MAT run. Confirm StressbalanceSolution and Vel, then choose Render.
The enabled button changes while the retained native velocity field is rendered.
steps.why: Render updates the retained native field without rerunning the model.
steps.expected: Expected: the accepted MAT run’s 13-node velocity field.
steps.note: This Results identity belongs to the accepted MAT run; the final native field contains 13 vertices and 16 triangles.

steps.title: 11. Inspect final native velocity
instructions: This is the unchanged native PNG from the accepted archive, with full axes and colour bar.
Speed is 100–180 m/year, and Vel agrees with hypot(Vx,Vy). The initial and solved velocities need not match in the interior.
steps.why: Use the full axes, colour bar and velocity components together.
steps.expected: Speed 100–180 m/year; Vel agrees with hypot(Vx,Vy).
steps.note: The mesh spans 10 km × 10 km. This diagnostic run has no transient time axis.

steps.title: 12. Interpret the checks precisely
instructions: Arithmetic-node mean thickness is 402.307692 m. Node-RMS speed sqrt(mean(Vel²)) is 142.564238 m/year; convergence count is the scalar 12.
These metrics are not area-weighted.
steps.why: Arithmetic-node metrics differ from area-weighted triangle metrics.
steps.expected: Mean h 402.307692 m; node-RMS speed 142.564238 m/year; iteration count 12.
steps.note: Five inferred non-front boundary vertices match input vx/vy. Saved spc arrays remain opaque; this boundary check is an inference, not direct decoding.

steps.title: 13. Prepare the archive download
instructions: Choose Download results. When the fresh HTTPS link appears, use it to save this run’s archive.
The next step follows that link; the archive contains the native fields, figures, initialized arrays and provenance.
Click the fresh download link. The browser saved a 15-member ZIP with valid CRC.
Every file is byte-identical to the originally checked MAT archive. Keep the archive with its input, image and output hashes.
steps.why: The archive preserves fields, figures, initialization and runtime provenance. Keep the archive with its source, data, image and output hashes.
steps.expected: 15 CRC-valid members, byte-identical to the originally checked MAT archive.
steps.note: Download preparation uses the completed run’s retained results. One native execution; this cached download does not rerun the solver. Repeatability and accuracy require separate checks.
